Class GroveGpsAir530

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.grove.sensors.GroveGpsAir530
public final class GroveGpsAir530 extends Object
Reads the Seeed Grove GPS Air530 over its one-way UART output. The module emits NMEA 0183 sentences at 9,600 baud by default; connect its TX wire to the selected Grove signal pin, normally D2 on a GroveBaseShield.

The reader uses a software UART, so it does not consume the board's USB serial console or require an Arduino library. The sentence and position arrays belong to the caller and every operation is allocation-free after construction.

  • Method Details

    • begin

      public void begin()
      Configures the GPS TX pin as an idle-high software-UART input. Call once at startup.

    • readSentence

      public int readSentence(byte[] sentence, int sentenceLength, int timeoutMillis)
      Reads the next complete NMEA sentence, without its line ending, into sentence. Bytes before '$' are discarded so a call can start in the middle of the continuous GPS stream.
      Parameters:
      sentence - caller-owned sentence buffer
      sentenceLength - writable capacity in sentence
      timeoutMillis - maximum time to wait for the next sentence start
      Returns:
      sentence length, 0 when no sentence started before the timeout, or -1 when the sentence did not fit

    • readPosition

      public boolean readPosition(byte[] sentence, int sentenceLength, int[] position, int positionLength, int timeoutMillis)
      Reads sentences until a checksum-valid GGA fix is received and writes its values to position. Latitude and longitude are signed millionths of a degree, altitude is in centimetres, and the last two entries contain the satellite count and NMEA fix quality.

      The caller reuses both arrays between calls. The position is left unchanged when the timeout expires or no valid fix was received.

    • parseGga

      public boolean parseGga(byte[] sentence, int sentenceLength, int[] position, int positionLength)
      Decodes one checksum-valid GGA sentence into a caller-owned five-int position array.
